segments.t: In the agency office, Andrea urgently discusses a major movie budget problem with Mathias and asks for his help. We will hear it in French first, so don't worry about catching every word.
Mais il ne veut pas céder.
Let's go back through it. Mathias greets Andrea.
'Hello, Madam Producer...' Mathias teases Andrea with her new title. The key noun here means 'madam', anchored by its matching French article.
'You scared me.' She was startled by his sudden appearance. Andrea uses the casual singular 'you' with 'to have', showing close familiarity.
'Croissants.' He brought some pastries for breakfast. The key noun here means 'croissant', anchored by its matching French article.
'Oh, marvelous.' She is delighted by the food. A short, idiomatic conversational reply that keeps the exchange moving naturally.
'Long night?' He notices she looks tired. The adjective meaning 'long' takes its feminine form here to match the noun it describes.
'I studied the project.' She explains what she was doing. In spoken French, the little word before 'to have' drops its final vowel and attaches with an apostrophe.
'I reviewed the whole budget...' She spent the night looking at the finances. The verb meaning 'to have' pairs naturally with the noun for 'budget' in everyday conversation.
'The numbers do not budge.' She found no room for savings. Notice the classic French sandwich negation wrapping right around 'to move'.
'We are missing 6 millions.' They have a massive deficit. The key noun here means 'lack', anchored by its matching French article.
'Did you call Xavier?' He asks if she spoke to the director. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'to have'.
'Yes.' She confirms she made the call. The adverb meaning 'yes' gives the reply its conversational emphasis.
Mais il ne veut pas céder.
'But he does not want to give in.' The director refuses to compromise. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'to want'. Let's listen to the whole scene again.
Mais il ne veut pas céder.
Andrea realizes the budget problem is serious. When you watch the episode, listen out for the expressions meaning 'madam' and 'producer'. You'll catch them now. See you next time!
